claims.text: On donhang, a connection to a Service with no ready endpoints is refused at once: wget prints 'Connection refused' for broken-selector, whose EndpointSlice is empty. Stated as observed on donhang, not as a kube-proxy mechanism.

An EndpointSlice lists the addresses of a Service's Pods with whether each is ready; ready addresses are the ones a Service normally sends new connections to; a selector matching no Pod leaves no address.

claims.text: A Service's EndpointSlices are labelled kubernetes.io/service-name=<service>, so kubectl get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=<name> lists them; the control plane keeps them in step with the selector.

claims.text: The port listed in a Service's EndpointSlice is the port on the Pods (the resolved targetPort): broken-port's slice shows 80, the fixed broken-selector's shows 8080.

claims.text: kubectl debug <pod> --image=<image> -c <name> adds a temporary (ephemeral) container to a running Pod; it shares the Pod's network namespace, so the Pod's NetworkPolicies apply to its connections. The network tests therefore depend on neither --target nor --profile.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Debug Running Pods > Debugging with an ephemeral debug container; Concepts > Ephemeral Containers; Network Policies (policies apply per Pod)

claims.text: kubectl debug --target=<container> lets the debug container see the named container's processes; --profile=general picks the named set of settings general for the added container instead of kubectl 1.34's default, legacy.
claims.source_hint: kubectl reference v1.34: kubectl debug (--target; --profile: legacy, general, baseline, netadmin, restricted, sysadmin; default legacy)

claims.text: Without -i/-t, kubectl debug starts the container and returns; its output is read with kubectl logs <pod> -c <name>, and its state appears in the Pod's status.ephemeralContainerStatuses.

claims.text: An ephemeral container cannot be removed from a Pod once added; it stays in the Pod until the Pod is deleted.
